title: Find a free cool space on a hot day
summary: The Mayor's Cool Spaces map lists indoor places to rest and cool down, plus shaded outdoor spots with seating, drinking water and toilets.
details: Use the Cool Spaces map on london.gov.uk to find the nearest space
The map is live 1 June to 30 September each year, matching the heat-health alert season
Outdoor shaded spaces may still be very hot in hot weather
Cool spaces are not medical care: if someone is unwell from heat, follow NHS advice
For free drinking water on the go, the page points to the Refill app (more than 4,000 refill places in London)

title: How to keep cool at home in a heatwave
summary: NHS advice for getting through a heatwave, including keeping your home cool and checking on people at higher risk.
details: Stay in the shade, especially between 11am and 3pm
Keep curtains, blinds and windows closed in the day; open them at night when it's cooler outside
Electric fans help when the temperature is below 35 degrees
Drink extra fluids but avoid alcohol, caffeine and hot drinks
If a rented home is dangerously hot, your council's environmental health team can inspect it

sources.title: NHS: Heatwave, how to cope in hot weather

title: Spot heat exhaustion and heatstroke, and when to call 999
summary: What to do if you or someone near you is overheating, and the signs that mean it's an emergency.
details: Move them somewhere cool, remove extra clothing, give water and cool their skin
Heat exhaustion usually doesn't need emergency help if they cool down within 30 minutes
Call 111 if you're struggling to treat symptoms or need advice
Call 999 if they're still unwell after 30 minutes, are confused, have hot skin that isn't sweating, or have a seizure

title: Get heat-health and cold-health alerts by email
summary: UKHSA and the Met Office issue weather-health alerts when temperatures are likely to affect health. Anyone can register to get them by email.
details: Heat-health alerts run 1 June to 30 September; cold-health alerts run 1 November to 31 March
Alerts can be issued outside these seasons if conditions meet the criteria
Register via the weather-health alerting system page on GOV.UK
Check current alerts for London on the UKHSA data dashboard

title: Check London's air pollution right now
summary: London Air, run by Imperial College London's Environmental Research Group, shows a live pollution map and today's and tomorrow's forecast.
details: Live map combines readings from the last hour with pollution modelling
Forecast tabs for today and tomorrow
Sign up for the free daily air pollution forecast email
Apps and widgets available for checking on the go

title: Get a 3-day air pollution forecast with airTEXT
summary: airTEXT publishes air pollution forecasts for London, aimed especially at people whose health is affected by poor air.
details: Forecasts cover the next three days and are updated daily
The Mayor's office describes airTEXT forecasts by text, voicemail, email, app or online for vulnerable Londoners

sources.title: Mayor of London: Air quality alerts warn Londoners about pollution

title: Check air quality for your area and get pollution alerts
summary: The government's Check Air Quality service gives a 5-day pollution forecast for your local area, health advice and alerts.
details: Search your location to see the forecast for the next 5 days
Sign up for air pollution alerts for your area
Includes what you can do to reduce your exposure on high pollution days
Phone line: 03459 33 55 77, Monday to Friday, 8:30am to 5pm

title: What the Mayor's high pollution alerts mean
summary: On high pollution days the Mayor issues alerts shown at bus stops and on the Underground, with simple steps to cut pollution.
details: Alerts appear on all bus stop countdown signs and on the Underground
Switch off your engine rather than idling
Don't burn wood or garden waste on alert days
Look out for vulnerable neighbours

sources.title: Mayor of London: Mayor issues high pollution alert

title: Grant of up to £7,500 for a heat pump
summary: The Boiler Upgrade Scheme pays part of the cost of replacing a gas, oil or electric heating system with a heat pump or biomass boiler, in England and Wales.
details: £7,500 for an air source or ground source heat pump
£2,500 for an air-to-air heat pump
£5,000 for a biomass boiler
Until March 2027, an extra £1,500 for homes heated by oil or LPG with no mains gas

sources.title: GOV.UK: Apply for the Boiler Upgrade Scheme
GOV.UK: Boiler Upgrade Scheme, what you can get

title: Free insulation, heat pump or solar panels through your council
summary: The Warm Homes: Local Grant pays for energy-saving improvements to privately owned homes for lower-income households, arranged by your council.
details: Household income must usually be £36,000 a year or less (some exceptions)
Home must have an EPC rating of D, E, F or G and be privately owned (by you or your landlord)
Council surveys the home and may suggest insulation, heat pumps, smart controls or solar panels
Apply online or call 0800 098 7950; your council usually contacts you within 10 working days
Depends on your council having funding available

sources.title: GOV.UK: Apply for the Warm Homes: Local Grant

title: Energy supplier help with insulation and heating (ECO4)
summary: Under the Energy Company Obligation, energy suppliers fund insulation and heating upgrades for households on certain benefits or lower incomes.
details: ECO4 runs until 31 December 2026
You may qualify on benefits including Universal Credit, Pension Credit, Child Benefit or Housing Benefit
ECO4 Flex can cover households with income under £31,000; check if your council takes part
Contact any obligated energy supplier, not only your own
It's not a grant: you may be asked to contribute, so compare offers and use a TrustMark installer

title: £150 off your electricity bill (Warm Home Discount)
summary: A one-off discount on your electricity bill each winter for eligible households, usually applied automatically.
details: £150 off your electricity bill, paid to your supplier
Usually automatic in England if you're eligible
The scheme reopens in October 2026 for winter 2026 to 2027

title: Sign up for free flood warnings
summary: The Environment Agency sends free flood warnings by phone, text or email for flooding from rivers, the sea or groundwater.
details: Free service; sign up online or call Floodline on 0345 988 1188 (24 hours)
Does not cover surface water flooding
On a warning: move people, pets and valuables upstairs and turn off gas, electricity and water if safe
On a severe warning (danger to life): call 999 if in immediate danger and leave if told to evacuate
Never walk, cycle or drive through floodwater

sources.title: GOV.UK: Sign up for flood warnings
GOV.UK: What to do during a flood

title: Check current flood alerts and river levels
summary: The Environment Agency's Check for Flooding service shows live flood warnings, a 5-day flood forecast and river, sea, groundwater and rainfall levels.
details: See current flood alerts and warnings in England
5-day flood forecast from the Met Office and Environment Agency
Search river, town or postcode for the latest measured levels and trend

sources.title: GOV.UK: Check for flooding in England
GOV.UK: River, sea, groundwater and rainfall levels

title: Check your home's long-term flood risk
summary: Look up the long-term flood risk for your area, including surface water, which is the main flood risk for much of London.
details: Covers rivers and the sea, surface water, reservoirs and groundwater (where data exists)
Shows how climate change may increase flooding
Does not show whether an individual property will flood

title: Report flooding or a blocked drain
summary: Who to tell about flooding depends on the cause: your council for drains and roads, Thames Water for sewers, the Environment Agency for rivers.
details: Blocked public drain or flooded road: report to your council via GOV.UK
Overflowing sewer or burst water main: contact your water company
Main river or sea flooding: Environment Agency incident hotline 0800 80 70 60 (24 hours)
Power cut or electrical danger: call 105

sources.title: GOV.UK: Report a flood or its cause

title: Affordable home insurance if you're at flood risk
summary: Flood Re is a joint government and insurer scheme that makes flood cover in household insurance more affordable for higher-risk homes.
details: Use the 'Can Flood Re help me?' tool to check your property
Find a participating insurer on the Flood Re site
Claims on policies backed by Flood Re carry a fixed £250 flood excess

title: Thames Water hosepipe ban: what you can and can't do
summary: A temporary hosepipe ban is in place for Thames Water customers until reservoir levels recover.
details: No hosepipes, sprinklers or pressure washers for gardens, pools, cars, patios or windows
Still allowed: watering cans, water butts, washing a car with a bucket, reusing household water on plants
Exemptions exist, including for some disability or medical needs
Thames Water will lift the ban as soon as conditions allow

title: Hire a Santander Cycle
summary: TfL's bike hire scheme: pick up a pedal or e-bike at a docking station and return it to any other.
details: Hire with the Santander Cycles app or a bank card at the terminal, from as little as £2
Day Pass usually £3.50 for unlimited 60-minute rides
Rides over 60 minutes cost £1.65 per extra 60 minutes on a pedal bike, £3 on an e-bike
E-bikes need free registration and are hired through the app

sources.title: TfL press: Cycle Sundays (Day Pass pricing)

title: Unlimited buses for an hour with the Hopper fare
summary: Pay £1.75 and make unlimited bus and tram journeys within an hour of your first touch-in.
details: Bus fare is £1.75; the Hopper fare is applied automatically
Touch in with the same card or device on every journey
Daily cap on buses and trams: £5.25; weekly cap (Monday to Sunday): £24.70

title: Check if your vehicle meets ULEZ standards
summary: The Ultra Low Emission Zone covers all London boroughs. Check your number plate to see if you'd pay the daily charge.
details: £12.50 a day for vehicles that don't meet the standards
Runs 24 hours a day, every day except Christmas Day
Enter your number plate in TfL's vehicle checker

title: Free cycle skills training for adults
summary: Free on-road cycle training for adults who live, work or study in London, arranged through your borough.
details: Free for anyone who lives, works or studies in London
Sessions last 1 to 2 hours and are tailored to your skills
Bikes can be borrowed if you don't have one
Contact your borough's cycling or road safety officer to book; often run through schools for parents and staff

sources.title: TfL STARS: Cycle skills for adults

title: Check what you can recycle in London
summary: London Recycles, run by ReLondon (the Mayor and London boroughs), has an item search and guides to your local recycling service.
details: Search any item to see if it can be recycled
Find what your borough collects at home
Guides on recycling symbols, plastics and food waste

title: Get broken electronics fixed for free at a Restart Party
summary: Free community repair events where volunteer fixers help you repair broken or slow devices.
details: Free to attend
Find upcoming London events on the Restart Project events page
The Restart Project also keeps a London repair directory

title: Borrow tools and appliances instead of buying
summary: Library of Things rents out household items like drills and carpet cleaners from self-service lockers on London high streets.
details: Join online, reserve an item and collect it from a locker near you
22 locations; find your nearest on the site
Return it clean for the next neighbour

title: Waste less food at home
summary: Love Food Hate Waste has storage guides, use-up recipes, a portion calculator and a postcode lookup for food waste disposal.
details: Search storage tips for common foods
Use the portion calculator when cooking
Enter your postcode to see how to dispose of food waste where you live
